utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. There were a few preliminary matters. Yes, Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. There are a few matters which I'd like to deal with right away. The first one deals with P6660. I do understand that the excerpt now contains both the selected portion by the Prosecution and the portion selected by the Defence, and that the translation is now complete for that excerpt, which means that nothing opposes admission any further. Madam Registrar, P6660 is admitted into evidence. Then there was another matter about yesterday's -- one of the documents of yesterday. That was the notebook page with attached to it some text and with which -- about which we thoroughly heard the evidence of Mr. Savkic. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, and good morning. First, for the record, we grant that the document has been admitted in the Karadzic case as an exhibit. In his testimony in that case, Mr. Redzic confirmed that much but not all of the handwriting on the document is his. We specifically dispute the authenticity of the date, 13 April 1992, on the document. The transcript references for the points that I raised yesterday, Mr. Savkic's evidence, that he does not know whether anything was added to the document between its discovery and when he saw it, that he does not recall who he heard about it from, and that he does not recall whether he ever saw the original are at transcript pages 27149 and 27150. Separately, we submit that in the context of the entirety of the witness's testimony about it, the document has no probative value. For efficiency, I will leave the matter there and simply note that if the document is eventually admitted, we will seek to agree to a small number of facts related to it with the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, now apparently this page is now loosened from its original context. Is that original context known and does it shed any light on dates because often notebooks are written in a chronologically sequential order? Is there anything that would shed additional light on that? And, as a matter of fact, I'm addressing both parties whether anywhere the complete text of that notebook is available.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Not that I am aware of, and I take it from my friend's body language that he may not be either. But I would appreciate if he could confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, Your Honours. We also have no information as to the whereabouts of the entire document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And just to perhaps complete the beginning of my submission, Redzic's testimony, the reason I inquired about Bajram yesterday with the witness is Redzic's testimony was, in fact, what the herd had referred to. And I can give the transcript references in the Dr. Karadzic case if it assists the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But the Redzic testimony is not before us, is it? It's not in evidence. So, therefore, you're now giving evidence, Mr. Traldi, which you're supposed not to do, by explaining the reasons why you asked certain questions. It's an elegant way of trying to circumvent the rule, but it's still not what we expect counsel to do. At the same time, I can imagine that the date of Bajram at -- in that year is something, I think, parties could easily agree on because that is a fact which is not easily manipulated. I leave it to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber defers its decision on admission. Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that we have another question relating to this document, which is the translation issue, which became important because you think that the translation used was from the previous case. Should you think that we need additional verification of this document, and we can seek that, but we would like to have some guide-lines as to how to address this matter as a whole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you referring to 12 and 16 at the top of the page, Mr. Stojanovic, or did we raise any other concerns about translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. I think that we have also raised whether the term used was "inductor" or "a doctor," which, in my view, is quite crucial. And, also, the last word from Finale, which, according to the witness, is the name of a company, whereas, in translation there's a -- a brackets and question mark fisala [phoen] so if it is possible, we may try to verify which word is correct and to decipher what is actually written in the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's not a translation issue but, rather, a legibility issue. I would invite the parties to see whether they can agree on these items. That is, inductor and Finale or what is declared illegible by CLSS. And then also not a matter really of translation is that the 12 becomes 16 or 16 becomes 12, I've forgotten which way it went, seems to be an issue also that the parties would have no dispute about. So for the other two, try to agree on what the text tells us to the extent legible because if there's no original then, of course, a missing letter cannot be repaired. Does that give you sufficient guidance, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. Yesterday we tried to reach agreement, but my young colleague and I seemed to have agreed yesterday that we could not agree. Therefore, we left this issue open.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic flatters me but otherwise correctly sets out the results of our conversation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, age becomes an item as well, I see. That's bad for the Chamber. So you do not agree on inductor and do you not agree on the -- Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry, and I thought he was describing -- perhaps I had misunderstood our conversation. We don't agree about admission. We don't agree about the implication of the word "inductor." We hadn't discussed the translation which I'll look at and come back to the Chamber later today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because I encouraged the parties to seek agreement on what the text in the original reads rather than what that means. That's a totally different matter. Then, having dealt with those, I have a few items on my agenda but I'll leave them for a later moment. Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Mr. Traldi, if it's of any comfort to you, or to Mr. Stojanovic, when I was acting as counsel before this Tribunal, I was usually addressed as junior assistant at level P5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, when we dealt with P6660, I should have first --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- instructed Madam Registrar that first a new version of 30947, 65 ter, should be uploaded. It's now 65 ter 30947A, which is the document now known as P6660, and ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, no, the new version would be 65 ter 30947B. We had already an A version before. And it is this new version, 30947B, which is now admitted as P6660. Madam Registrar saved me through this dangerous cliffs. Good morning, Witness. Before we continue, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony, and Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And Mr. Jeremy will now continue his cross-examination. Mr. Jeremy, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours and good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And good morning to you, Mr. Pljevaljcic.

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning to you too.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: I'd like to start today by briefly discussing the command structure of your unit during the period that you were in Foca. So yesterday you told us that you were the commander of a company of 70 or 80 men. Now, your commander, the commander of the 5th Battalion, was Boro Ivanovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And this battalion was part of the Foca Tactical Group, yes?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, in June 1992, Marko Kovac was the commander of the Foca Tactical Group, yes?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Later in the war, the Foca Tactical Group was renamed the Drina Tactical Group, yes?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, Serb troops in Foca, including your company, were incorporated into the Army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina from late June, early July 1992 onwards, yes?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correctly. Approximately as of the 28th, which is St. Vitus Day.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, at this time your battalion, the 5th Battalion, became part of the 2nd Foca Light Infantry Brigade; correct?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: I'd like to turn now to briefly discuss an operation that your brigade participated in while you were still in the army before your injury in -- in mid-July 1992. Now, in paragraph 6 of your statement, we read that, "We had no ambition to capture territory towards Gorazde." Here are you referring to your company, to your battalion, or to your brigade? Could you specify who you mean by "we," please.

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was primarily referring to my company. Yesterday I said that whenever the Muslim horse -- forces attacked in order to recapture the lines towards Foca, we retaliated fiercely. And Cerova Ravan was captured on -- on about the 12th of July which is two days before I got wounded. And on that day we lost two fighters. I also believe that an order was issued to launch a ferocious attack against them. That's why we captured Cerova Ravan on the 12th. And then early in the morning of the 13th, they attempted a counter-attack to retrieve --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please slow down. Interpreters are unable to follow and we'd like to know what you tell us. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So in the early morning hours of the 13th, they attempted to carry out a counter-attack but they failed. On the 14th, at half past 4.00 in the afternoon, they launched another heavy attack and we did not suffer any losses. And I'm saying that my company occupied Cerova Ravan on 12th of July, 1992, and my company remained there until the Dayton. I did say yesterday that there were some counter-attacks before and after I had left the unit, but the essence is, and the fact is, that we arrived at Cerova Ravan on the 12th, and we remained there until the Dayton, virtually in the same place.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, Witness, thank you for that answer. I would now like to show you a couple of documents that I think are related to this ferocious attack you refer to. And I'd like you to confirm whether those documents are indeed related to that attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we please see P3680 on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Pljevaljcic, on the screen before you is an order dated the 6th of July, 1992. It's from the Main Staff of the Army of the Serbian Republic of BH. It's sent to the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps Command for information and to the Command of Serbian forces defending Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we please go to page 5 in the English and page 3 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And, sir, we see here that this order is type signed by General Mladic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we please go back to page 1 in each document. Each translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Witness, in paragraph 1 of this document, we read in pertinent parts: "Due to the offensive operations and successes of our forces in the general sector of Foca, Sarajevo, Vlasenica, Rogatica, Visegrad, Srebrenica, and Pale, the Muslim Ustashas, withdrawing before the strike of our forces, are grouped in a large mass in the general sector of Gorazde."

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, could we please skip forward to page 3 in English and page 2 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Witness, on the page before us, I'd like you to focus on paragraph 5: Tasks for the units. And could we --

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I don't have it. Item 5, you said?

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Item 5, yes. Tasks for the units. And I'd like to focus on (b). So could we go forward one page in the English. So directing your attention to 5(b), this reads in pertinent parts: "The Foca Tactical Group shall use forces up to the strength of one brigade and reinforced artillery to attack the general Ustikolina-Gorazde access axis ..." Witness, this is the -- this order is -- it's connected to the operation that you have just referred to in your previous answer; correct?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is a connection. And in this period, the territory of Foca municipality had not yet been liberated. I told you yesterday that we had decided to liberate the entire municipal border of the municipality of Foca. Cerova Ravani is precisely on the line between Gorazde and Foca but that was not the case on the 12th. It says here from Ustikolina towards Gorazde. Our line went as far as Ustikolina and took the lines Zebina Suma and Prebila [phoen]. And this is where they stayed until the Dayton Accords were signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, in connection with this order, I'd like to show you another order, also, I believe, related to the same operation. I'll ask you to confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we please see P2823.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Sir, on the screen before you we see an order from the Foca Tactical Group. It's dated 7th of July, 1992, so the very next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: If we could please go to page 5 in the English and page 6 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And we might have lost that document for a moment on your screen but we'll have it back shortly. While we're waiting for that, Witness, I'll ask you, do you recall -- actually, it's on the screen before us. So we see that it is signed by Marko Kovac, your brigade commander, and we see there is an instruction there to send to all subordinate units. Do you recall receiving an order in connection with these operations on -- on this date, on the 7th of July, 1992?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is similar to the first one. I didn't see it then. My battalion commander probably saw it and probably had a document like this. It was emphasised in the first paragraph, as far as I could notice, that there were large groupings of the Muslim forces and everything else that I've already told you about. We had carried out an attack in order to reach the line, and that was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we go back to page 1, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Pljevaljcic, we see that the title of this order is: Order from the commander of the Foca Tactical Group to break through the siege of Gorazde. I would like to focus your attention on paragraph 2 of this document and the first sentence where we read in pertinent part: "With one brigade reinforced by artillery, the Foca Tactical Group shall attack in the general Ustikolina-Gorazde direction?"

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we please now go to page 2 in the English and the B/C/S. I'd like to focus on paragraph 5, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And, sir, in paragraph 5, we see a reference to the 2nd Foca Light Infantry Brigade with instructions to attack a particular location. So your brigade and your units were involved in this attack that we see was ordered by General Mladic and, in turn, by Colonel Kovac. Yes?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the order, but I know what happened. That is what I'd like to deal with a bit. I've already told you, I see the order, I was aware of that order, but a few days before this attack, on practically all the lines, we had three of our soldiers who were killed, two Blagojevics, and Grujic, the commander of a company. And then what followed, followed. And in this way, we completed the defence line of Foca. Probably in some areas we went even further, but at any rate, the line, the administrative line, was kept throughout.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: I'd like to move to page 3 in the English of this document, and I'd like to look at the top of page, page 3, and page 3 in the B/C/S. I'd like to focus halfway down the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, sir, halfway down the page in the -- in the B/C/S version, we see a reference to the Serbian Army Miljevina Battalion. That was Pero Elez's units, yes?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Pero Elez's.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, Radovan Stankovic was a part of his units, yes?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Radovan Stankovic was convicted by the court in BiH in 2006 for rapes and abuse of women in Foca, yes?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know he was convicted, but that has nothing to do with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we please go to the next page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, we see a reference to the 1st Independent Dragan Nikolic detachment. That's at the top of the page in the B/C/S and halfway down the page in the English. Sir, in July 1992 this detachment was commanded by Branislav Kosovic, yes?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not Kosovic, Cosovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you and forgive my poor pronunciation. Now this unit included Zoran Vukovic, Radomir Kovac, also known as Klanfa, and Janko Janic, also known as Tuta, yes?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who was in that unit. I was not in that unit and I don't know who was there. I know all of these men, but whether they were in that unit ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall testifying in the Karadzic case in January 2013?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And do you recall being asked about these same men and whether they were in this particular unit?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. Maybe a question was put to me but I really don't know what the point is whether they were there. They were in the Army of Republika Srpska. Now the least important thing is in which unit somebody was. I mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Refrain from commenting on what is important and what is not important. Limit yourself to answering the questions. It may be very important for us even if you do not understand that. Please proceed, Mr. Jeremy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Witness, in the Karadzic case, when asked about these three men, you said that, "I think that they were in this unit." Would you provide the same answer today?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I'd give the same answer. I think they were. But I'm not claiming that with certainty. That's an assumption only.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, both Zoran Vukovic and Radomir Kovac were convicted by this Tribunal for rapes against women in Foca, yes?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know they were convicted, but I don't know what for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jeremy, for the basis of all this -- Witness, you said, I would give the same answer. I think they were members of that unit. And you then added: "That's an assumption only." Now, on -- why do you think that they were members of that unit? You must have a reason for that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I would see them. You know what? Even when defences are carried or attacks or whatever, we act together. So then soldiers mix. So I am just assuming that they were in Branimir Cosovic's unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say you worked together with that unit, and you saw them -- when working together, you saw them at the time which makes you think that they may have been members of that unit. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is well understood. You understood that, that this operation, the taking of Preluca [phoen], et cetera, we were there together. Now whether they were in that unit or in Gojko Jankovic's unit, that I don't know. But I did see them. They were there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Jeremy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Sir, you've talked about working together with these units and below the reference that we just looked at to Dragan Nikolic, we see a refreshes to the independent Zaga detachment. And we read that it shall take part in the "ciscenje," cleansing or mopping up, of inhabited areas in the direction of the 5th battalion's attack. So that was your battalion and this is an example or this is an order for your unit to work with the independent Zaga detachment, yes?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, something like that. Zaga had a very small unit, five or six men, and he was involved in reconnaissance and he was very good and reconnoitring. He provided us with information. That is strictly what he did. He was a reconnaissance man. And it wasn't even a platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And, sir, when you refer to "Zaga," you were referring to Drago Kunarac; correct?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And you know that he was also convicted of crimes in Foca, including rape, by this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know he was convicted, but what he was charged with, I don't know. I didn't read any of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, you said that Zaga was involved in reconnaissance and in connection with this man and his duties, I'd like to show you a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we please see 65 ter 31461.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, sir, on the screen before you, we see a -- a certificate in respect to Drago Kunarac. We see in the top left corner that this was issued by the military post 7141 Srbinje on the 16th of July, 1999? Now we read below that that the certificate was issued at the request of Defence counsel for Drago Kunarac. In the body of the document, we see a reference to offensive operation ordered on the 7th of July, 1992, by the commander of the Drina TG. So that's the operation set out in the documents that we've -- we've just looked at; correct?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And we see a reference to combat in this area commencing on the 9th of July, lasting until 21st of July. And we see a reference to the Cerova Ravan elevation. That's where you were injured during this operation; correct?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And in the final paragraph we see a reference to the reconnaissance duties that Mr. Kunarac carried out during that operation. Those fit with the description that you provided you of this man's duties; correct?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tender that document as the next Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31461 receives number P6842, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, there's no objection. We admit it. P6842 is admitted. At the same time, Mr. Jeremy, I've never heard a military post telling me anything. An unknown person signing this -- well, it's true that it seems that it fits with the testimony of the witness, but the Chamber has -- at least I and perhaps my colleagues would also have some questions about what this actually means. But I leave it to that for the time being. So probative value is still to be carefully considered. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, sir, a few minutes ago you mentioned that you knew who Radovan Stankovic was and that he was a member of Pero Elez's unit. Now, in connection with this man, I would like to show you a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we please see 65 ter 27944.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Sir, we see that this is an order dated 7th of April, 1995. It's from President Karadzic to the VRS Main Staff. And it concerns the transfer of a group of conscripts from VRS units to the Ministry of the Interior in order to form detachment of special police forces in Srbinje. Sir, you know that Foca was renamed Srbinje, yes?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for a certain period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And you know that Srbinje labelled Foca a Serb place, yes? That's what the name means.

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not right. That is not right because it had to do with the other towns in Herzegovina: Nevesinje, Ljubinje, Trebinje, Srbinje. You can rest assured that it was on account of that. It rhymed better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was it just for rhyme that it would fit better with Trebinje as -- what does Trebinje mean? Literally.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well I don't know what it means. That something is needed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What does Srbinje mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, then it meant the name of the town. Now whether it meant something to anyone, I don't know. To someone obviously it meant that it was Serb. I know, I was there, I was a citizen of that town when the name was changed, and I know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You said to someone. Obviously it meant that it was Serb. To someone? Or to those who changed the name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I mean Muslims. And later, in the joint parliament of the municipality of Srbinje, at their intervention, the name was reverted to Foca. So they were bothered by it. Well, I can say that a few Serbs were bothered by it too, a few Serbs who were also in the municipal assembly. But the majority had voted in favour of it at that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why were they bothered if it's just rhyme? I mean, good rhyme is good for everyone, isn't it? Or were they bothered because it was such a clear reference to Serbhood, that new name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, somebody sees it that way. But other people see it the way I had put it. I was a member of the municipal assembly, and I was one of the people who was against that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, whether you were in favour or you were against, that's a different matter. But you say it was just for rhyme and that was why some people were bothered about it, others were not bothered about it, so poetical issues rather than whether it referred to Serbhood. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you again: That's really what you mean? It's about rhyme. It's not a reference to Serbhood in common understanding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Jeremy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could we go to page 2 in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, sir, here we see a list of military conscripts who are reallocated in the VRS to the MUP in order to form a detachment of special police forces in Srbinje. Number 1, we see Radovan Stankovic, son of Todor, detachment commander. Sir, you -- you are aware that Radovan Stankovic became the commander of this special police in Srbinje; correct?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did know that. But, believe me, I didn't know Radovan Stankovic personally until he came to prison at the KP Dom. But I did hear about this unit. I know that it had been formed. And I don't see what's in dispute. I mean, concerning the establishment of that unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, don't bother about whether it's important or not, what the issue is. We leave that to the parties and the Bench will consider that. You don't have to give any comment on that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. And I tendered this document as the next Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 27944 receives number P6843, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Sir, to finish today, I'd like to discuss briefly your evidence relating to the partisan hall and to the KP Dom facility. Now, in paragraph 14 of your statement, you say that when the conflict broke out, some Muslim inhabitants had to be accommodated and that is why they were placed in Codor Mahala, the partisan DTV, and KP Dom. Now, as regards the partisan hall or DTV, you never actually went there, did you?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, certainly, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: All right. Well, we'll leave that there. Now in respect to KP Dom Foca you started working there in 1995; correct?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, did you ever go there between 1992 and 1994?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't go there. I was passing by, as I went to the hospital, because I was wounded. And I did pass by the KP Dom because you do pass that way if you go to Cerova Ravan and that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Sir, this Trial Chamber has received evidence of beating and killings of non-Serb detainees in KP Dom between 1992 and 1994. My question for you is: When, if at all, did you first learn about these beatings and killings at KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally never did. I'm telling you, until July, I was at the front line. I wouldn't leave the front line for 25 days, stretches as long as that. And then what happened --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, would you focus on the question. The first question was: Did you learn about beatings and killings in KP Dom. That means not whether you observed it yourself but whether you learned about that. Did you, or did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if I say yes, it would be yes, in terms of from the media or following trials, reading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you say yes, so you learned about them. When did you learn about them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I learned about that when the first people of Foca were arrested and when the trials started. Then it was mentioned that that did happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean after the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes, after the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jeremy, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Sir, your -- your brother Vlatko was a guard at KP Dom, yes?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. He is retired now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And he worked there between 1992 and 1994, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From time to time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, this Tribunal, in the Krnojelac case, found that your bother was implicated in the beating and killings of non-Serb detainees in KP Dom. That's paragraphs 317 and 339 of the Trial Judgement. You know that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I haven't read the Krnojelac Judgement. And knowing my brother, I don't believe that. That's for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Sir, you've told us today that you only became aware of these beatings and these killings at KP Dom after the war. Now, since your brother was a guard at KP Dom during the relevant period between 1992 and 1994, I put it to you that you knew about these beatings and these killings at the time that they were happening.

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard of it. I never read about it. I didn't have any knowledge about a single Muslim becoming a victim at the KP Dom. I didn't hear a thing like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic, it's time for a break. How much time would you need after the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Probably around five minutes, not more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We could consider -- if you say it's really five minutes -- and I'm looking at my colleagues. It seems that we have no further questions for the witness. We could consider to use that five minutes now. But I leave it to you and to Mr. Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, it's better if we continue so we release this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'll now be re-examined by Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning once again, Mr. Pljevaljcic.

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have briefly P3680 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While we are waiting for it to come up, it's a document signed by General Mladic. It's dated 6 July 1992. And in connection with this document, a document produced by the Foca Tactical Group was shown to you dated the 7th of July, 1992. It concerns an order to carry out operations towards Gorazde. You told us that you stopped at the administrative line with Gorazde. Were there any requests on the part of the soldiers in your units to go ahead and proceed?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were such requests.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What kind of explanation was given?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were such requests because Miroslav Stanic was the chief of the Crisis Staff, and therefore he was probably involved in all of this. When we occupied these lines, the Serbian army had such a level of morale that they wanted to advance, and we asked Stanic to allow us to advance towards Gorazde. However, he said, I spoke to Radovan Karadzic and he told me that the administrative line of Foca municipality should remain. And that's what we did, although the soldiers were very much keen to proceed, and they put forward such requests.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the Muslims have good sabotage elements who came behind your backs?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, most probably, judging by the actions they carried out, and it happened almost on the regular basis. December 1992, Josanica, then Jabuka, then the villages around Tjentiste, then Selo -- village Brigovinija [phoen], Slatina. These were the places where all these sabotage groups made incursions into, committed atrocities even against the children. There are monuments commemorating these victims and there were over 100 of them. However, no one has been prosecuted for that crime to this date.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You have been asked about members that you say might have been members of Dragan Nikolic. Do you know if these were permanent members? Did they used to go to and fro? Did they act independently? What do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These people were involved and that's why I said they might have with Dragan Nikolic. They were sometimes with Vojko, sometimes with volunteers from Serbia and Montenegro, so these people were switching from one unit to another. They were looking for a suitable environment for themselves. There's no doubt that once they engaged in combat, they were remarkable fighters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pljevaljcic. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: TRIVKO PLJEVALJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jeremy, no further questions for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Pljevaljcic, this concludes your testimony in this court. I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague. It's a long way for you. And I would also like to thank you for having answered the questions put to you, put to you by the party, put to you by the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break, and we resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the Defence ready to call its next witness? Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think so, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. In view of the time estimates, we should give it a serious effort to finish, to conclude the evidence, of this witness today. Thirty minutes for the Defence; one hour and a half for the Prosecution. That should fit within -- until quarter past 2.00. Otherwise, the witness would have to wait until after the weekend. Good morning, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I think, to be accurate, our estimate was about one hour, which is what I will try to stick to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's even before, I would say. Then I must have missed something, because I have still one hour and 30 minutes on my list but could be that it has been corrected afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: It is possible. But I am hopeful we'll be able to finish this witness today in any event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. And perhaps even start with the next one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Mladjenovic. Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration. The text is handed out to you. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mladjenovic. Please be seated. Mr. Mladjenovic, you'll first be examined by Mr. Stojanovic. You find him to your left. Mr. Stojanovic is counsel for Mr. Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, Mr. Mladjenovic, good morning.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please state your full name for the record, but slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Miladin Mladjenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mladjenovic, have you given a written statement to the Defence team of General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we have in e-court document 65 ter 1D01669.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mladjenovic, since this is your first appearance here, please look at the left-hand side of the screen in front of you, and there you can see a text. My question is: The details, personal details contained herein, your name, your date of birth, name of your father, your nationality, and the signature, is that all yours?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at the last page of this document. Mr. Mladjenovic, on this page that you see in front of you, have you put the signature and the date in your own hand?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And one more question. Can we please now focus on paragraph 7 of this statement. You will have it in the B/C/S as well, so paragraph 7. Sir, during proofing for your appearance in this courtroom today, did you point out to me a typo in the last name of the person mentioned in paragraph 7. So that instead of "Milicevic," it should read "Milovcevic"?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now that we have made this correction for the record that you indicated, today, since you made a solemn declaration, would you give answers in the same manner today as you did with regard to the questions put to you in this statement, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we please have the statement of Mr. Miladin Mladjenovic, 65 ter 1D01669, tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D1669 receives number D707, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honours, I would take the liberty to read the summary of this witness's statement.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We only have a B/C/S version. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The interpreters tell us that they only have a B/C/S version of your summary, but if you slowly read, Mr. Stojanovic, it will work.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct. Thank you, Your Honours. Until the 1992 war, Witness Miladin Mladjenovic, worked as a driver for Vihor company based in Bratunac. After the outbreak of war, he was recruited as a member of the civilian protection in the village of Kravica, since he had earlier been wounded at Mount Majevica so that practically he was unfit for military service. In July of 1995, he worked as a gatekeeper in the Vihor rolling stock compound and he remembers that after the fall of Srebrenica, he received an order from his supervisor to take a company bus and to drive Muslims to -- from Potocari to Kladanj. After he took the bus, he went to Potocari, and on the road, he saw a number of buses heading for Bratunac. Upon arrival in Potocari, in front of a house in the vicinity of a transformer station in Potocari, he boarded his passengers, namely, women, children, and elderly men, and drove them to Tisca village located on the separation line with the Muslim forces. From that point, the passengers continued on foot towards the territory under the control of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. He did not make any other rounds on that same day. The next day, following an order of his supervisors, he came to Potocari again at around 9.00 and drove men fit for military service from Bijela Kuca, the white house, the whole day. He took them to the gym inside the elementary school in Bratunac, and according to his calculations, he made around ten rounds and drove between 450 and 500 people. In front of the gym, he saw a policeman from the Bratunac police station, but he didn't see any senior officers. The witness does not remember whether anyone else gave a ride to these people in Bratunac except him. He received information in Bratunac that these able-bodied men that he had driven there would be transported to Kladanj. During the boarding of the bus and within the area around the white house, he did not see anyone being beaten or maltreated. When he finished work on that day, he thinks that the white house was completely vacated. On the following day, he went back to his regular duties in the company where he worked. Now, this was the summary of this witness's statement, and with your leave, Your Honours, I would put just a couple of questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you do so, please give me one second. Yes, please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mladjenovic, could you please tell the Court how far is the village of Tisca from Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly what the distance is, but I know that it took four to five hours to drive because I was not alone on the road. There were convoys and convoys of buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is that the time of one-way trip, this four or five hours, or is it a return trip?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: That was the duration of a return trip.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the first day, when you drove those people, was it necessary for you to stop anywhere along the route?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I stopped in Vlasenica, and when we were approaching Tisca, they were thirsty and we gave them water.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Will you tell us, please, for how long did you stop and remain in Tisca village?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we spent quite some time there because we were waiting for these convoys to pass so that the road can be cleared.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness please repeat how long they stayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you notice any abuse, any maltreatment? Did you see anyone being separated from their family?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, the interpreters did not catch how long the witness said they were waiting for the convoys. How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean while we were waiting in Tisca?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Between half an hour and one hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we please now focus our attention on paragraph 5 in the document, which is now marked as D707, where you say speaking about the first day that you travelled to Potocari, and you say: "I went to Potocari on the way there, I saw several buses that were going in the direction of Bratunac." In order for us who are not from that region to have a clear picture, can you please tell us and give us approximately a more precise location on the road between Potocari and Vlasenica or Bratunac, where did you approximately encounter these vehicles?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I saw some of them en route from Bratunac to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Court the distance in kilometres between Potocari and Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: About 3 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from buses in that convoy, did you see any other kind of vehicles that were used for transportation?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: There were some heavy-duty vehicles, such as lorries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I seek clarification, Mr. Stojanovic. Sir, you're quoted as saying that you saw the buses en route from Bratunac to Potocari. Was it Bratunac to Potocari or Potocari to Bratunac? According to the statement, you said from Potocari to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Since I went from Bratunac to Potocari, I encountered buses and trucks, driving from Potocari towards Bratunac. That is to say, towards Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would ask you to tell the Court about that first day. What is your best estimate? When did you leave those people there and when did you go back to Bratunac? What day was that?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: That was approximately 1700 hours in the afternoon, and I returned to Bratunac around 7.00, 7.30, in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My last question is going to be similar. Can you tell us approximately at what time you finished driving to Bratunac on the following day, the next day, the last time you went to Bratunac and the elementary school.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: That was approximately 1600 hours. I don't know the exact time, but around 1600 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you set out towards the school in Bratunac, did anybody stay behind at Bijela Kuca, the white house, as you call it?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: When I dealt with the last transportation, the white house remained empty. There was not a single passenger left.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mladjenovic, for your help.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I put one follow-up question to the last one. You said there was not a single person -- a single passenger left in the white house. How do you know that? Did you leave the bus and enter the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And which part of the house did you visit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ground floor and upstairs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And while you were visiting the white house, the last passengers were already in your bus. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I went to check, to see whether anybody was left behind. I checked. There was no one left there, and that's how we set out towards Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And the last passengers were already in the bus while you were visiting the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Were there any guards guarding the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What type --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had one military policeman who was with me on the bus.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And were there any other uniformed people around the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I also have one question. In your statement, we read that you said: "While the men were entering the bus," you're talking about the day when you arrived at 9.00 in the morning in Potocari, "I did not see any of their personal items." Do I have to understand this as they did not carry any personal items?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not search these military-aged men. They didn't have any kind of luggage, no bags, nothing like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you see, when going out of the bus, did you see any luggage near the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just one question.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Thank you, too, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What uniform were these guards wearing who were guarding the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Military uniform of which army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the Army of Republika Srpska. Camouflage. It was a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, are you ready to cross-examine the witness, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I would like to introduce you to the witness first. Mr. Mladjenovic, you'll now be cross-examined by Ms. Hasan. You'll find her to your right. Ms. Hasan is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Mladjenovic.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I would just like to start with a correction to your statement. Now, in your statement, at paragraphs 4 to 5, you describe the first day when you picked up -- or you took a bus and you transported women, children, and elderly men from Potocari to Tisca. Now, did you transport the men, women, and children on the 12th of July, that first day, on a bus?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Do you recall testifying about this very subject matter before the State Court of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the Dusko Jevic case?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And before testifying in that court, you gave an oath to tell the whole truth?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Do you -- and that what's you did?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But I had just one correction.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I addressed the Court because I kept thinking, and it seemed to me that it was on the first day that I drove the women and children and men who were not fit for military service in a truck.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So today do I understand that -- am I to understand you that you drove the women and children and elderly men on a truck?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I drove a bus. Well, I kept thinking -- since there were a lot of buses and trucks, I kept thinking it was a truck. But what is correct is that it was a bus that I drove on the first day.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, you were ordered from your house to go to the Vihor company to pick up the bus.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we could take a look at 65 ter 31477.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: This is -- what you'll see is an aerial image of Bratunac. And take your time to look at it. What I'm going to ask you to do is to identify the Vihor company premises for us.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And, meanwhile, if I could ask the usher to provide the witness with a marker.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could somebody please explain this picture to me because I'm not very knowledgeable about this kind of thing?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Well, Witness, this is an aerial image so it's an image taken from a bird's eye view of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you can see on the -- the top centre, do you -- can you identify the stadium there?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: The thing with the white lines; is that it?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Just next to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we -- could we --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we seek the assistance of the usher moving a pointer so that we are better able to -- could we just -- Ms. Hasan, if you say, Do you see this and this, could you ask -- could the instruct the usher to move the pen or whatever it is, the pointer, at the issue you wanted to look at. Stadium, for example, may I take it it's a little bit further to the right as from where it is now?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: That's correct. More to the right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: More to the right.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: It's right there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you see an oval there, Witness, an oval next to where that pointer is? Could you please refrain from marking yet. Could the markings be undone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Uh-huh. All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you see an oval?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what Ms. Hasan refers to as the stadium.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Perhaps it might assist if we just blow that up, the centre of that picture up a little bit, to see if this helps the witness orient himself. That's a little bit too much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we zoom out again.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Does that help you, Witness?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could you put an X on the premises of the Vihor company.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I think, Your Honours, that that's it, this photograph that I marked.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, you picked up the bus on the first day and the second day from -- from those premises; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Where did you get the fuel for your vehicle from?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: At the company, Vihor Bratunac, within the compound of the company.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: All right. Now, if you left the company, are you able to show us using arrows the route you took from Vihor to Potocari, the road that you took?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could you just -- at the end of the line you have just drawn, can you put an arrow and write a letter P, for Potocari, so we know the direction.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And when you transported the women and children to Tisca, you would have taken the road to Konjevic Polje, is that correct, towards Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could you just mark -- mark with the letters KP the road that leads to Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd offer this marked aerial image into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31477, as marked by the witness, receives number P6844, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now I'm going to show you, Witness, a very similar aerial image. It's perhaps a little bit closer than this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 4826 displayed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, we know this image was captured on the 12th of July, 1995, at approximately 2.00 p.m. Do you see there on the road a lineup of buses in the centre of that image?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. We can try to zoom in a little bit. Do you see them now? There's some buses lined up there just in front of the Hotel Fontana.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see it now.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, when you -- in your statement, you say you left to pick up your bus from the Vihor company between 1.00 and 2.00 p.m. When you drove to Potocari, did you see this lineup of buses?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: These buses were not only from Vihor Bratunac. These buses came there from Zvornik as well, buses and trucks, that took over -- I mean, Muslims and drove them to Kladanj. It wasn't one or ten buses. It was like 50 or even more buses and trucks.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Do you -- do you know whether some of those buses were Sarajevotrans buses?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, I take it you're familiar with the Hotel Fontana. Were you aware that earlier that morning, on the 12th of July, that General Mladic had a meeting at the Hotel Fontana?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know because I wasn't there. I worked on that day. I was at work.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Just to go back to your -- the evidence you gave to my friend earlier today. You said that you went to Potocari at 5.00 p.m. and that the transport took until about 7.00 to 7.30 p.m., so I just want a clarification of what you did between 1.00 and 2.00 p.m. and 5.00 p.m.?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am talking about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- the first day --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll first listen to Mr. Stojanovic. Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm afraid that this kind of question is going to create confusion. Whether it's the first or second day, that is my first point. And secondly, I think that it is a misquote. The witness did not say the time that is denoted here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's what the witness said. Ms. Hasan, having heard the concerns of Mr. Stojanovic, are you able to rephrase your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Well, I'll go back to what was asked of the witness and that was, "I would ask you to tell" -- this is transcript page 32, line 9: "I would ask you to tell the Court about the first day. What is your best estimate? When did you leave those people there and when did you go back to Bratunac?"

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry. So if I understand you correctly, Witness, 5.00 was when you left the women, children, and elderly men at Tisca; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, around 5.00. Because I don't remember the exact time, so it's around 5.00, in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. So between 2.00 p.m. and 5.00, you're travelling to Potocari and you're loading up people waiting for the convoy to depart?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd offer 65 ter 4826 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document receives number P6845, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived Potocari on that first day, who directed you as to where you should be parking your bus?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Those guards told me, the ones that were up there.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And when you say "guards," are you meaning soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: These were VRS soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Soldiers of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So let's move onto the 13th of July, the second day when you went back to Potocari. Now this is when you -- when you transported the separated men from Bijela Kuca to the sports hall of the elementary school in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we could take a look at 65 ter 31478, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And we see here that this is a -- another aerial image of -- sorry. An aerial image of Potocari that's captured at about 2.00 p.m. on the 13th of July. Witness, are you able to orient yourself and tell us where, if you could mark with a B, the direction where the road leads to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot find my way in this picture. Could somebody please explain this image to me?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. Do you -- do you -- can you identify the DutchBat compound?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we first enlarge a bit more because ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm just interested in where Srebrenica is and where Bratunac is. Is it here or up here? And that way I can orientate myself on this picture.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Well, I can tell you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if the parties agree on -- we see a road which stretches from the top to the bottom, where it appears that there are quite some vehicles which, from the air, look as if they may be buses. Now, direction up, would the parties agree what direction that is?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: That's Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's Srebrenica for the Prosecution. And for the Defence as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence agrees that that's the direction towards Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And south is the direction?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I say south, I say bottom. That's Bratunac. Now, what is -- do the parties also agree on what is north and what is south?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: North is in the direction of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So, therefore, that's -- may create quite some confusion, that usually maps and aerial images are giving north up, and south down, and where this is just the opposite way. Is there any way that we could turn this 180 degrees? Witness, could you have a look again? Now, up to the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Up to the top is north and goes in the direction of Bratunac, whereas, down is now south, and that is the direction of Srebrenica. Does this assist you in --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then carefully listen to Ms. Hasan's questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, are you able to identify on this aerial image where the house was that you picked up the separated men from?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I think that it is this house here.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Have you marked something on the map? Can you -- can you draw a circle around it.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I think that it's this house here, this circle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you mark that -- I see no marking yet.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the witness has now marked.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And I take it's the house that's just at the tip -- the top tip of that circle you've drawn?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, can we --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Actually, can I have this marked image entered into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31478 as marked by the witness, receives number P6846, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could I ask that we zoom in closely onto the area of the house the witness has just marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In this document with the marking or in the document without the marking?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Either or.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I suggest --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: That works --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that we zoom in in P6846 so that the witness knows where he has marked. Could we zoom in the lower part. No, I want -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That takes a minute. But I think it would assist the witness in -- especially if we zoom in, that he knows where he made any marking. Ms. Hasan, is this --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: That'll do. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So do you see a bus that appears to be parked, or at least in this image is captured, just on the road next to that house?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I can see the buses, but I parked my bus within the grounds of the house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you perhaps first answer Ms. Hasan's question. There is a -- apparently what may be a line of buses all from top to bottom, but just above where you marked, there is a short, white feature which is not in line with the others but is more right/left oriented than up/down. Do you see that one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Shall I mark it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you just tell us whether you see that this one feature --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- seeming to be a bus which is, I would say --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So, in fact, when you picked up the men, you drove closer than that to the house?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd ask that the original aerial image which bears the date and time also be admitted into evidence, the blank one, so that we preserve that information as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it not yet in evidence as part of a bundle?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'm not sure which bundle, Your Honour, you're referring to. It's not -- that date and time is not in Jean-Rene Ruez's book, if that's what you had in mind. A similar --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I had a book on my mind, indeed, but ...

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: There is a very similar image. It does not bear the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then what -- we also could ask the witness to write on this picture so that we have the information together. Could you write in this picture: 13 July, 2.00 p.m., because that's what you would like to have in evidence. Or am I wrong? When I'm wrong, I leave it to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I leave it in your hands whether you want to have -- I think it was 65 ter 31478, to have that additionally in evidence mainly in order to see date and time.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31478 receives number P6847, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, what is P6846?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The -- the same picture just marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. -- well, I'm looking at the clock. It's -- it's about time to take a break. But, first, Witness, we'll take a break, and we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we take that break, Ms. Hasan, forgive me, we have been away for quite a while from Srebrenica and Potocari, but you asked the witness to mark how he went with his bus from Bratunac to Potocari, and then you later asked him how -- what route he would take to Konjevic Polje. Now, he marked the exit road of Bratunac in -- if that at least is also north/south directed, to the left upper direction.
