Now, could you tell me whether that picture, that aerial picture, whether that is also reversed as far as north/south is concerned, or is that correctly oriented? That means, north up, south down.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I believe that that's reversed as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's reversed as well. That would result -- if that's the case, that might resolve my problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you check that during the break, and I'll tell you why I would like to know that. Because up and left would, in a normal orientation, be north-west; whereas, from what I understand from the maps, until now, Potocari is, rather, south from Bratunac than north-west. So I wonder whether the marking of the witness is reliable in terms of whether a road leads at all to Potocari in that direction. Could you please verify that during the break and inform the Chamber after the break. We take that break and we'll resume at 20 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted in the courtroom. Meanwhile, Ms. Hasan, could you inform us about the aerial image you've shown to the witness in Bratunac whether top is north or south or neither of them. That's also a possibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: It's -- it is actually neither of them. It's a little bit complicated to turn that particular photograph. But what I can tell us is that the witness has correctly marked the roads, the directions I've asked him to, that Potocari is in the direction of south-west. That's the first road he marked. And Konjevic Polje, the second road that he marked, is in the directions -- is west. So it's south-west and westerly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And we've checked that with the Defence, and they agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then I'm always confused whenever aerial images are turning around --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And it may of some assistance, our map book, which is P1087, on page 17 is correctly oriented, and you can see the two roads that he's marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'll do that. Your map book, do you have the P number for that, so that's ...

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, that's P01087. And the relevant is page 17.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: On the second day when you transported the separated men from the white house to Bratunac, how many MPs were on the bus that you drove?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: One police officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Were these members of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And, sir, you -- you said there was one and I take it these were military police, Bratunac brigade military police?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: When you say "these," it's a little --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- bit confusing if there was only one.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: There was one.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I will take you, Witness, just back to your testimony that you gave in the Dusko Jevic case. And you've told us that you confirmed that you told the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we could have -- see 65 ter 31479A, please. This is an excerpt of the transcript of the witness's testimony before the State Court. If we can -- that's the cover page. If we can turn to page 2, please, in the B/C/S and English.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If you take a look at -- it's going to go from page 2 to 3 in the B/C/S. In English, it's on page 2, and we can see at line 5: "Was anyone escorting you at that moment towards the school in Bratunac?" "Witness" -- if we can turn to page 3 of the B/C/S, please. And your answer was: "There were two military policemen. Question by Defence counsel: "Were they members of the Bratunac brigade?" Your answer was: "Yes." So, Witness, can you tell us which is correct what you told the State Court that there were two military policemen or what you're telling us today, that there was just one?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Both are correct because sometimes there were two of them, and sometimes there was one of them because I made more than one round. So either is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, these MPs, either one or two, they escorted you at all times when you were travelling; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Sometimes one of them would get off, just to have a meal or something. But basically they were with me all the time. Sometimes one will stay behind, and sometimes both of them, we -- would travel with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Do you have their names?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know their names. No, I don't know. I just know them by sight.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Was it the MPs, then, who also told you to drive the separated men to the elementary school/sports hall?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we received our orders in Potocari, and we were told where to go. They just accompanied me. It was not their role to issue any orders. Other people did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Who told you to drive the men to the school in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: The guards who were at Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And by "guards," you mean soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: VRS soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And when you arrived at the elementary school in Bratunac, it was the MPs had instructed the prisoners to go into the sports hall?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: As they were disembarking, there was a civilian policeman there, and he would be there to escort them into the gym.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, the separated men that you transported from Potocari, were they all led into the sports hall of the elementary school?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And I'll ask you to turn your mind back to Potocari for a moment on that second day when you were transporting the men, did you see men - Muslim men I'm talking about - on the balcony of the white house?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And throughout the day, 13th July, when you're going back and forth from Potocari to Bratunac, at no time did you see belongings, bags, the personal belongings, outside the white house on the ground?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'd like to show you a video.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we could have P1147. That's the Srebrenica trial video. It's ERN V000-9267. And, for the record, the clip will begin at 0010 -- ten minutes and 20 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No text, Ms. Hasan?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: No. For the purposes of this question, we won't be relying on any text. I don't believe there is any text in this portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: We can stop it right there. So for the record --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you don't use text, then also the sound should be switched off because the witness would hear that, and that's ... But please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So, for the record, the video is stopped at 00:10:47.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I can tell you that that video was taken the afternoon of 13th July. And you recognise the white house there, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you still maintain that you didn't see those men on that balcony?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you also claim that you missed the -- the mounds of belongings that were outside the white house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if there had been so many belongings on the ground, I don't know how I would have been able to park my vehicle close to the white house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, if you say, You claim that you missed, I think the witness said that he didn't see it. He didn't say that he missed it. Because if you say, I missed something, then you acknowledge that it was there but that you oversaw it. If you say, I didn't see anything, that leaves it open whether there was anything there or not. And I do understand that it's the Prosecution's position that there was something there, but in all fairness to the witness, claiming that he missed something is not what he said. He said, I didn't see. It's a slight difference, but I insist on precision in this respect. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, when you transported the -- these men from the white house, did any members of DutchBat in UN vehicles escort your bus on any of the trips that you made between Potocari and Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Did any UN vehicles follow the bus that you drove?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: When you arrived at the elementary school in Bratunac, approximately how much time would you say you stayed there before returning back to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Between 15 and 20 minutes at the most. Maybe up to half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And did you see any UN vehicles or any members, DutchBat officers, there in the vicinity of your bus?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. In Bratunac or in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I apologise. I wasn't very clear. I would like to know whether you saw DutchBat officers or DutchBat vehicles in the vicinity of your bus when you arrived at the elementary school in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No, they were not there.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And, sir, would you agree that it is possible that there were other drivers, other buses, that were transporting separated men from the white house in Potocari to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'm going take you back to your testimony in the Dusko Jevic trial. And that's 65 ter 31479. And, again, if we could turn to page 2. Yes, I apologise. If I didn't say so, it is 31479A, the excerpt of the testimony, and page 2 in the English, page 3 in the B/C/S. At line 26 in the English, we see that you were asked by Defence counsel: "But you would agree with me that you, according to your information, were the only one who was transporting those men by bus on that day?" And your answer was: "That is possible." And then Defence counsel asks you: "You did not see anyone else doing that? And your answer was: No. So, Witness, you told the Court, the State Court that it was possible that you were not the only one who was transporting the men by bus from the white house on that day?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, it's just the opposite. The answer relates to the question if he was the only one. And he said that is possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: That's absolutely correct that it's possible he was the only one.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And I take it from that that it's possible that you were also not the only one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Your Honours, I believe that this is a deduction made by the Prosecution rather than a question. She read a portion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course it is deduction. If you say it is possible that it rains, then it means that you're not certain and that, therefore, there's a possibility that it doesn't rain. That means you can't tell. Now, the same if you say it's possible that I was the only one, you leave it open that you were not the only one. So, to that extent, it is -- I do agree with you that it's a deduction, but it is not a deduction of facts. It's a deduction on possibilities, which is not the same, and perhaps we make it clear to the witness -- You said at that time, as it was read to you, I didn't see any others. And you said it's possible that you were the only one. Now, do you consider it possible as well that you were not the only one, even though you didn't see any others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I claim that I was alone and that I only transported Muslims fit for military service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you mean that you didn't see anyone else doing it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, even if you do not see something to -- happens, it's still possible that it happens, or do you have any specific reason why you can exclude for certain that another bus or -- was involved in a similar activity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, and as far as I remember, there was no other bus.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There was no other bus in your recollection. Please proceed, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we could briefly move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before we do so, let me put one follow-up question. You have still the transcript of the other trial in front of you, and the question which was put to you there first was the following. I quote: "You cannot tell us whether you were the first one who had transported the group of people to the school or was it somewhere -- someone else." Your answer was: "I can't tell you." I take it that, at that time, you couldn't exclude that somebody else was driving a bus too; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Hasan. And we first move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You mention in your statement that you recognised a colleague of yours from Fakovici or from somewhere around Srebrenica who worked in Vihor as a truck driver with you before the war. Was he one of the men that you transported from the white house to the elementary school in Bratunac, to the sports hall?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Have you seen him since then?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Did you make any efforts to locate him and find out where he was or what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I did not make an effort, and there was no need for me to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Do you recall his name today?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't remember it even then, when I spoke to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to see if I can help you refresh your recollection as to who this person was. Now, there's a driver from Fakovici, and his name is Hamed Hasanovic. Does that help you refresh your recollection as to whether that was the man that you -- your colleague?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot recall. I just knew the face but not the name.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, on the days following, following the 13th of July, were you involved in any of the transportations of prisoners to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No. After the 13th of July, I returned to my job as a guard, because I actually had work obligation.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you -- when you say you returned to your job as a guard, was that at the Vihor company compound that we've seen?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I was over there at Borkovac where those old vehicles were. That is at the entrance from Kravica towards Bratunac, if you remember, on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So when you -- on those day, the 14th, 15th and 16th, did you ever go back to Potocari or Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we take a look at 65 ter 31490, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: This is a report from the Bratunac public security station. It's dated the 2nd of October, 1995. And it's reporting on the work of the department in the month of September 1995. If you take a look at paragraph 1 -- sorry, item 1, it provides: "Mladjenovic, Miladin, aka Miso, son of Savo and mother Todora, nee Obakcic, born 10 October 1960 in Mratinjici municipality of Bratunac, permanently residing in the settlement of Redzici, municipality Bratunac." Is that you?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And it goes on saying: "Married, father of two, without prior convictions." And it says that you were deployed to work detail as porter at TP, which is transport company Vihor, in Bratunac. And it says: "Because there are reasonable grounds to suspect that he committed the crime of aggravated theft from the Article 148, paragraph 2, of the KZ," and we can turn to the next page in the English," of the penal code of the RS by discovering and appropriating two large truck tires on wheels and large number of brand new spare parts for trucks and buses, the value of which is around 10.000 dinars, from deserted Muslim houses in the settlement of Potocari, municipality of Srebrenica, on 14, 15, and 16 July 1995." So, sir, is that what you were doing on those dates?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: That did happen, but I don't know on which days. Was it a day or two or three or ten or 15 days? Well, it's correct. As for those two tires, I didn't take that from Potocari. I took that from the company where I had worked as a -- as a gatekeeper.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And on the 13th of July, in the evening when you returned, did you return your bus to the Vihor company compound?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And as you drove through -- into and through Bratunac, did you see buses and trucks parked in several locations around the town, including in front of the municipal building, in front of the Vuk Karadzic school, and in other areas?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Possibly. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Did you see trucks parked right in front of the Vihor company garages?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: We had 400-something buses and trucks altogether.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Did you -- when you returned your bus to the compound, did you see trucks parked in front of the garage which were loaded with Muslim prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, there's evidence before this Chamber that there were trucks carrying prisoners that were just parked outside the Vihor company and that prisoners were taken off these buses. Screams and shots were heard, and that the prisoners did not return to the buses, that these shots were regularly heard throughout the night and well into the morning. So did you -- I should say this: It's the Prosecution's position that men were taken off these trucks and killed right outside the company. So did you -- were you aware of this? Did you hear these shots?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I did not say that the buses and trucks were full of passengers. I said that they were empty trucks. I mean, it's possible that they were empty, but I did not hear of any passengers there so the buses were there. They certainly weren't full. I would have heard.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Hasan. Any further questions, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just briefly, Your Honour. With your leave, perhaps it would be fair if the witness had been shown something, to show what time this was when this testimony referred to this happening, when putting one's case to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What night --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can do whatever you think Ms. Hasan didn't do and you find appropriate to do rather than to tell what Ms. Hasan did wrong. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try to deal with it this way then.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Witness, did you spend a single night at the Vihor company during those days, mid-July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No. I've already said where I was, a gatekeeper.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And one more question in relation to that. One part of the Vihor company, did it have its premises in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: That wasn't Vihor. That was Srebrenica Ekspres.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now could we take a look at this together, document P6847. Mr. Witness, can you see here the white house that you marked on that enlarged image?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Are there several approaches or only one to the white house?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but I just know of this entrance, from the asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The entrance into the compound of the white house, as we call it, how far away is it from that road?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps 2 or 3 metres. I don't remember exactly. Something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I will conclude by putting the following question: To the best of your knowledge, with regard to this terrain, was it possible to access the white house from anywhere else with a vehicle like a bus?

utterances.speaker: MILADIN MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think so. I think that would be impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mladjenovic. We have no further questions for you. And thank you on behalf of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, any further questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladjenovic, this concludes your testimony because the Prosecution and the Bench have no further questions for you. I'd like to thank you very much for coming a long way to The Hague and for having answered the many questions that were put to you by the Prosecution, by the Defence, and by the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's a little bit early to take a break. Therefore, I'll use the time to deal with a few matters. I'll start with the references to the term "balija" in English translations. On the 14th of October of this year, during the testimony witness Milenko Jankovic, the Defence requested the redaction of the remark, and I quote, "derogatory term for Bosnian Muslims" next to the term "balija" in the English translation of Exhibit P1064 admitted into evidence through Witness RM513. The Chamber then informed the Defence that it would verify the practice it had adopted when a similar matter had arisen in the case. The Chamber notes that the issue has been discussed in court on different occasions, in particular, on the 30th of May, 2013, Witness Momir Nikolic, and on the 4th of September, 2013, Witness Richard Butler, in relation to similar remarks added in English translations of documents containing the terms "balija" or Turks. The Chamber further observes that the Defence has not systematically objected to the addition of such remarks in English translations. For instance, the English translation of Exhibits P1091 and P1064 admitted into evidence through Witness RM015 on the 27th and the 28th of February, 2013, both contain the remark, and I quote, "derogatory term for Bosnian Muslims" next to the term "balija" and although the characterisation of the term was discussed with the witnesses in court, the Defence did not formulate any objection concerning the English translations at the time of their admission. When seized with objections of that kind, the Chamber has accepted the practice of CLSS when encountering words either untranslatable or where a literal translation would be inadequate in the context in which the word was used an English explanation in slash brackets is then added after the original words. This system alerts the reader that the English version of the text is to be understood in the context as assessed by our professional interpreters. The explanation, therefore, does not mean that the word has exclusively this meaning, but that the interpreter considered that this explanation provides the best understanding of the word in its original context. When CLSS explains the word "balija" in official documents as derogatory term for Muslims, the -- this does, of course, not exclude a different use of that word in a different context. It's well known that words which in another context would be considered to be offensive are sometimes also used in warm and affectionate relationships with a totally different connotation. The practice of CLSS puts the reader on notice of the contextual interpretation or explanation of the term used and any party may challenge the translation or interpretation in that given context. That the word has several meanings or is not always used with the same connotation is not in itself sufficient to ask CLSS to strike the explanation it considered to be appropriate in the given context. This was the guidance of the Chamber and the review of the practice developed before this Chamber. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, for addressing this issue after you. But I think that on that translation we could see draft translation. So we want to check also whether it was translated by CLSS or by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine. That's a different matter. But the core of the issue, of course, is -- and, of course, you could have it verified if it is a draft translation. I must admit that I've seen so, so, so many documents with a draft translation mark on it that if you want to review them all, that's fine. But I understand you're busy already, Mr. Lukic, so, therefore, I would not encourages you to do it. And, second, apart from draft translation or not, I think it was an official document, and the context seems to be clear. You can check whether the original word is "balija" and then what remains, apart from verifying the translation, is a discussion on whether this explanation is adequate in the given context. That's the issue we are looking at primarily. Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: We've just verified that, in fact, the document mentioned is a CLSS translation. Sorry, CLSS draft translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If Mr. Lukic considers it necessity to have it reviewed on whether a final translation would give the same results then, of course, he is invited to do so. But let's try to be focussed on what raised the issue, that is, that interpretation or explanation of that word in that context. And let's focus on that, to start with, because I didn't hear any other objections about the translation at that point in time. I leave it to you, Mr. Lukic, whether you want to give it a follow-up and have this specific portion be verified. Then I briefly address another matter, which is about a corrected version of Exhibit P2586. On the 25th of September of last year, 2013, the Trial Chamber admitted into evidence, under seal, excerpts of the testimony of Witness RM026 from the Prosecutor versus Stakic case. The Chamber notes that the document uploaded in e-court under Exhibit P2586 contains the excerpts admitted into evidence, as well as excerpts of another witness's testimony. The excerpted admitted into evidence under seal as P2586 are: Transcript pages 2303, line 13 up to 2303, 16; 2325, line 16 to 2325, line 21; 2334, line 25 to 2336, line 21; 2343, line 25 to 2345, line 10; and 2387, line 19 to 2392, line 9. The Chamber hereby orders the Prosecution to upload a new document with the correct transcript pages under a new 65 ter number, and we suggest 30368a, and instructs the Registry to replace the existing document uploaded as P2586 with the corrected version uploaded by the Prosecution under the suggested number, 65 ter 30368a. And that concludes this observation. Is the Defence ready to call its witness after the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, we are, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that would then be ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It would be Mr. Rajak, Milenko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajak. Yes. We'll take a break of 20 minutes and we'll resume at 20 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Rajak.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The text of a solemn declaration will now be handed out to you and I'd like to invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Mr. Rajak. Mr. Rajak, you will first be examined by Mr. Lukic. You'll find him to your left. Mr. Lukic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Mr. Lukic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Rajak.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Will you please slowly state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: Milenko Rajak.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Also please make a pause after I finished my question in order to allow the interprets to interpret.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Must give a good feeling that someone is trying to contact you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I apologise. My phone rang.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have in the e-court 1D1700, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Rajak, do you see on the left-hand part of the screen that it is written: Witness statement?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Have you given a statement to General Mladic's Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this document before you, do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Whose signature is that? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: It's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at the last page.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: Yes, we can.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you see a signature on this last page?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Whose signature is that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: It's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please look at paragraphs 9 and 10, page 3 in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rajak, when you and I met, did you bring to my attention that you wished to make some corrections in these two paragraphs?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before we proceed with the corrections, what was the reason for your not having it corrected before you signed it? Can you explain us briefly.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: That was due to my health condition. Since I was wounded, I had to go to a -- the infirmary to be given shots as kind of painkillers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When did you sign the statement -- I mean, when was that, with regard to the signing of statement?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is the relation between the statement, the signing, and your receiving injections?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: Well, the lawyers came to see me, but I didn't have time for them. I was sick. I had to go to the clinic and that was the reason why I failed to correct paragraphs 9 and 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, did you drive yourself to the medical institution or were you driven by someone?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: My son drove me there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, first, I would point out there is only difference in between B/C/S and English translation and in regard of war criminals in paragraph 9. In B/C/S, it says "Prisoners of war." So that's one of the corrections. Only in between the translation and the original document. It's in -- in the line 2 of paragraph 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It says in the original, "Prisoners of war."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If that's the case then -- of course, I'm a bit surprised that the witness tells us that the translation is wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That was what I found. He found something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I noticed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He corrected the place --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- is recorded wrongly, so instead of "Veljko Vlahovic school" it should Rasadnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay, that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's clear. That's paragraph 9?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. And then paragraph 10 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In English it's not that visible, but in B/C/S it is obvious not the full sentence here. Somehow it was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Could we --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- blacked out, so I could read how that whole paragraph should read. The sentence -- the second sentence: "Vlahovic and Rasadnik were outside its purview and under the control of the Rogatica Brigade." And there should be three sentences instead of this. And it should read: "I do not have any knowledge about its competencies, it's work or its composition. Rasadnik was partially under TO/military control, and partially under the police control. Veljko Vlahovic school was under the control of civilian authorities."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, yes, but to present this as not being complete where the meaning changes 180 degrees is at least, Mr. Lukic, is a euphemistic approach because whether they were under the brigade's control or not may make quite a bit of a difference. And then to say, of course, it's not complete, well, it's far more than that. You are aware of that, I take it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In B/C/S if the translators can see, it's really not a complete sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I'm not saying that it's complete.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's why the meaning is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A part, "the brigade," is now out, and in that respect, I would say it changes, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It said, "Rasadnik was partially under TO/military control. "

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Originally it said Vlahovic and Rasadnik were under control of the Rogatica Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And now certainly they are partially under TO. Is that then still the Rogatica Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: TO -- until 22nd of May it was under TO, and after 22 of May, 1992, it was army. That's how the witness sees it, and I think it is in accordance with the documents we have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It doesn't say anything about what happened after the TO/military control. It does not directly link it to the brigade any further. But let's see whether -- Witness, when you said in the new version Rasadnik was partially under the TO/military control and partially under the police control, did you include still the Rogatica Brigade as partly being in control?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I included that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That clarifies certainly some matters. I take it that you want to proceed with the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- in order to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So do you want me to read the full paragraphs corrected or it's not necessary?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I think if you do not tender the new version, then, indeed, you should read the -- you should read them -- read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So paragraph 10 should read: "The Crisis Staff was formed at the end of May/beginning of June, after the negotiations with the Muslims, who had actual power, failed. I do not have any knowledge about its competencies, its work for its composition. Rasadnik was partially under TO/military control and partially under the police control. Veljko Vlahovic school was under control of civilian authorities. There were various civilian and military authorities and one could not give orders to the other. Responsibilities were not mixed."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's now the new text. Does the lack of knowledge appear in the original one, or is it not? Or is that added?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's added.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's added.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Then I take it you want to further deal with the requirements for admission?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Rajak, after we have made these corrections, is everything else contained in your statement accurate and truthful?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: Yes, it is accurate and truthful.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I were to put the same questions to you today, would you essentially give the same answers as you did when you provided this statement?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm now going to read the summary of your statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you seeking the statement to be admitted --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No objections, Mr. President. Just for the clarity of the record, we'd request that the witness be asked if he confirms the corrections as read by Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you'd -- well, perhaps to cut matters short, the corrections that were read to you by Mr. Lukic, do you agree that those are the corrections you intended to make?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D1700 receives number D708, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D708 is admitted. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. It will be very short statement summary. Rajak Milenko was born on the 3rd of February, 1965, in Rogatica. Witness was member of Territorial Defence in Rogatica in April 1992. In May 1992, he became a member of Rogatica Brigade and he was in the 2nd Infantry Battalion of Rogatica Brigade. He will testify how Serb forces in Rogatica were self-organised on principle of Territorial Defence. Same case was with Muslim population, and they also organised in those areas where they were in majority. He will testify on clashes between Muslim and Serb forces in Rogatica municipality, on establishing control over city and Rogatica municipality. He will testify on particulars regarding event when he was wounded on 14th of July, 1992, during clashes with Muslim forces, and, after 1993, he became a member of military police in Rogatica Brigade. Witness will confirm that he has no knowledge on any illegal order whatsoever issued in his unit. And, Your Honours, I would have several questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Rajak, have you recently sent three documents to the Defence team of General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What did you send to us?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: I sent you the records relating to the fallen fighters, to the military invalids, and the civilian casualties of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which post are you holding nowadays?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: I am the president of the veterans' association of Rogatica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you professionally fully employed in that position?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please have 1D3953 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What we see in front of us is a list of the fallen combatants with the dates when they were killed. Do you know where -- when the list of the fallen combatants were -- was compiled?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: Yes. These lists were updated on a daily basis. Company record keepers kept daily record of the numbers of combatants which gave us information about how many of them were killed and how many were wounded. So we had the situation day by day, and on that basis, we knew how much -- how many more combatants we needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were wounded on the 14th of July. Were there any fatalities on that day among members of your unit?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: Yes, four of my fellow combatants were killed on the day when I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you remember any of their names?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: I know their names. Ljuban Coric, Miso Mladen Ikonic, Milija Rajak, and Milenko Lazic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have page 5 in this document on our screens. The lowest part of the page, number 60.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Which page in English?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's -- I thought it's the same page in English, fifth page. We need number 60.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Number 60 in sequential order --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Page 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- appears on page 10 in e-court in English, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was just -- was just sent for translation, so I didn't have English versions in my hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So number 60, is that one of the men that you mentioned, among the men who were killed on that day when you were wounded?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see the next pages in both versions, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The people who were killed on the same day when you were wounded, where are they on this list? Which numbers?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: Sixty-one, 62, and 64.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This list, how did you compile it? Did you make it or was this a list that had already been completed? Just tell us how it was that we received it.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: From the database, from the computer. I got this list from there. It's been in existence since 1993 when the veterans' organisation was established. And that means that every day records were kept on the combatants who had been killed. Since we did not have the proper technical facilities for that, we had to use typewriters at the time. So later on, we transferred all of this to a database in the computers that we have now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, yes, I have one question. Under number 64, the date is the 14th of June, and that's also the date in the original so I have some difficulties in understanding that that also happened on the 14th of July. Have you any explanation for that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: Yes, possibly this is a typo. But it's certain that it was the 14th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean you remember that person being killed on the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. He was right next to me, a metre away from me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Can we see the last page of this document, please. And we have to see that the right -- bottom right-hand corner in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Rajak, can you recognise the signature that we see on this document?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: Yes, I can recognise it. It is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we would move and tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No objections, Mr. President. I understand that the Defence is also seeking to add this and the other two to their 65 ter list and we wouldn't object to that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First we have to -- my colleague is right because we just received the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have first to ask the admission of this document under our 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could you tell us the relevance for the case because I -- I don't know whether the Prosecution intends to provide us with list of fallen soldiers because this case is not about fallen soldiers. Mr. Lukic, this case is not about fallen soldiers, even how deplorable it may be that they have fallen, but, of course, I've some concerns that if we come up with lists of all the soldiers that died in -- even up to January 1996 in Sarajevo and even some of them, I think, in 1991 in -- that -- any -- what is it that you intend to establish by this? Or is it just background?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We -- it's a background. And we, by this way, impeach the statements of the Prosecution witnesses that they claim that there were no fightings. There were -- in -- in that area. They were not armed. We want to say that all the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but who were not armed? Who were not armed?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And fightings. Sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Who were not armed?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Some of the witnesses, like -- I cannot mention him name and I don't know his number by heart, said that there was no resistance in Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Well, I do understand that you want to deduce from this list that they were killed by members of the opposite in combat of opposite forces in combat. Okay. That's clear. There's no objection. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D3953 receives number D709, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The next document is in regard of wounded, so -- but I will have one question in regard of that document as well. If we could have document 1D3952 on our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Rajak, this is a list of disabled war veterans and it is compiled on the basis of date and place of wounding. Is this your list?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are all the wounded persons on that list? And what was the criterion used to put a person on this list of wounded persons?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: Not all wounded persons are on this list. It is only the veterans whose level of disability that had been established that are on this list, but there are many other veterans who had lighter wounds and who are not on this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do any of these people address you or any of the family members of the persons who had been killed?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why do they address you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: Well, the veterans' organisation is the port of first call, if I can put it that way. They can address us so that we could help them exercise their rights on the basis of the law that deals with war veterans in Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see the last page of this document shortly, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Rajak, do you see the signature there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Whose signature is this?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: My very own.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the stamp? Whose stamp is that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: The stamp of the veterans' organisation of the municipality of Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are not going to deal with this document in depth because we have time constraints, but I'd just like to ask for another document, 1D3962. This is a list of civilian casualties from the war of the municipality of Rogatica. Who compiled this list, Mr. Rajak?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: Also the veterans' organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see the last page. Do you see the signature and the stamp here?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise them?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: I do. My very own.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would just like to tender these two documents now as well and we wouldn't have any further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As with the first, no objection either to their addition to the list or to their admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If we admit into evidence certain documents which did not appear on the 65 ter list, it is implicit that we have granted leave to add them to the list. One little question perhaps, Mr. Lukic. You said for the previous one, and I'm talking about the list of wounded now, that you sought to establish that there was combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mm-hm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, glancing through the two lists very briefly, it struck me that the list of the dead was, well, let's say, almost exclusively people who died in Rogatica, whereas for the wounded, they are wounded many, many different places, so I wondered to what extent that adds to establish that there was combat in the Rogatica, if you are dying in Vogosca or in other far-away places. Probative value for that is -- is that a different one or ... I'm just trying to understand what I'm supposed to look at.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... translations so the witness has your full question, actually. I would [overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But it's a question to the -- it's a question to the Defence, not to the witness, because the probative value is not something the witness -- could Mr. Mladic sit down. He would like to consult you, I take it, but I would first like to have an answer on my question, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Lukic, I asked you to first answer my question and then I give you an opportunity to consult with your client.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rajak, how did that happen? As can you see on the list of the wounded persons, people were wounded in different locations. How come your municipal veterans' organisation of Rogatica is -- has them on this list?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK
utterances.text: Exodus. People who came from Sarajevo, Vogosca, they had their names recorded with our veteran's organisation so we have records of these persons who are temporarily staying in Rogatica now and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. Mr. Lukic, you apparently have not understood what I have asked you. If you give us a list of people killed, all recorded as having been killed in Rogatica, I understand, and I ask you to explain that. I understand that this may add to evidence that there was combat in Rogatica. What I've difficulties in understanding, if you come with a list of wounded people who were wounded everywhere, that that would contradict what witnesses said about combat in Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would withdraw our request to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we don't have to decide on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... should be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we still -- there's one document remaining. That's the list of --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- civilians that were killed. Any objections? No objections. Madam Registrar, for that list which is -- let's me just see. That's --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D3962.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That would receive number ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives number D710, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Witness, we'll not be able to conclude your evidence today, unless the Prosecution would refrain from cross-examination, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. I need about half an hour, I am afraid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Need about half an hour. Witness this means that since we're not sitting on Friday, that we'd like to see you back on Monday morning at 9.30 in this same courtroom. Meanwhile, you're instructed that you should not speak or communicate with whomever about your testimony, whether that is testimony you have given today or whether that is testimony still to be begin on Monday. If that is clear to you, you may follow the usher, and we'd like to see you back after the weekend. No loud speaking --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I just saw in this text a mistake. This should be corrected, the year when I was born at the very beginning of the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We'll look at that. What is your date of birth? Your year of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1965. And it says 1964 at the very beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's hereby, then, corrected. Well, we now that now for the weekend. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: With the apologies to all those who are assisting us. Mr. Lukic, on the statement of the witness, it says 1965.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says 1965, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was it that he appeared on the list of wounded that he corrects something which is not finally not in evidence? Could it be that he is listed there with a wrong date of birth? Well, perhaps you look at it and we now know forever that it was --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is on that list that is not admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then the correction is fine but not very relevant, nor needed. I wish everyone a good weekend. We adjourn for the day, and we'll resume, Monday, the 27th of October, in this same courtroom, I, at 9.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 27th day of October, 2014, at 9.30 a.m.
